title: R-MEL: Recovering Contrastive Signal from All-Negative Groups via Prefix-Primed Revision

contributions.purpose: Identifies that all-negative trajectory groups in RLVR contrastive methods (~30% of training compute) are discarded and yield no learning signal.
contributions.mechanism: Characterizes the all-negative waste problem in GRPO/MEL-style contrastive learning and proposes prefix-primed revision as a principled solution.
contributions.evaluation: Motivated empirically by the observation that approximately 30% of training groups are all-negative during early training.
contributions.source_quote: We identify the all-negative waste problem in RLVR contrastive methods and propose prefix-primed revision as a principled solution.

contributions.purpose: Recovers contrastive learning signal from all-negative groups that would otherwise be discarded.
contributions.mechanism: R-MEL truncates failed trajectories at candidate bifurcation points and generates correct continuations; pairs passing verification with sufficient prefix overlap are used for standard MEL meta-experience construction.
contributions.evaluation: Converts discarded groups into useful training data without additional rollout compute; validated on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
contributions.source_quote: We introduce R-MEL, which recovers contrastive signal from discarded groups by truncating failed trajectories and generating correct continuations.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrates that recovering all-negative groups improves reasoning performance over the MEL baseline.
contributions.mechanism: Trains with R-MEL and compares Pass@1 and Avg@8 against MEL and other baselines across five math benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: R-MEL achieves 33.17 average Pass@1 (vs MEL 33.00) and the highest Avg@8 (30.78) across all conditions, outperforming baselines on 3 of 5 benchmarks including a statistically significant +4.0 percentage point gain on MATH-500.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that R-MEL achieves 33.17 average Pass@1 on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, outperforming the MEL baseline (33.00) and achieving the highest Avg@8 (30.78) across all conditions.

contributions.purpose: Characterizes when prefix-primed revision is most beneficial.
contributions.mechanism: Analyzes revision success rate as a function of prompt difficulty, revealing an inverted-U pattern.
contributions.evaluation: Intermediate-difficulty prompts show the highest revision success rate (15.4%).
contributions.source_quote: We reveal an inverted-U pattern in revision effectiveness: intermediate-difficulty prompts show the highest revision success rate (15.4%), providing insight into when prefix-primed revision is most beneficial.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Our work differs from these approaches by specifically targeting the all-negative waste problem in RLVR, using prefix-primed continuation to recover contrastive signal while maintaining the meta-experience learning framework.

Meta-Experience Learning (MEL) (Huang et al., 2026) further refines this approach by constructing meta-experiences from trajectory pairs and internalizing them into model memory... when all sampled trajectories fail verification (all-negative groups), no learning signal is available and the group is discarded.

notes: Pass@1 improvement over MEL baseline is marginal (33.17 vs 33.00); the paper itself notes it outperforms baselines on only 3 of 5 benchmarks, a partial/near-tie result. Revision success rate is low overall (peak 15.4%).
